question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.2$ |

Calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint support $S$ is defined as

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y).
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.4$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.7$ | $0.3$ | $1$ |

We now compute $\text{E}[X]$ and $\text{E}[Y],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & =2\cdot 0.4+3\cdot 0.6 \\  & =0.8+1.8 \\  & =2.6 \\ \text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =1\cdot 0.7+2\cdot 0.3 \\  & =0.7+0.6 \\  & =1.3\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for the covariance, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])(y-\text{E}[Y])f(x,y) \\  & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}(x-2.6)(y-1.3)f(x,y) \\  & =(2-2.6)(1-1.3)f(2,1) \\  & +(2-2.6)(2-1.3)f(2,2) \\  & +(3-2.6)(1-1.3)f(3,1) \\  & +(3-2.6)(2-1.3)f(3,2) \\  & =(-0.6)(-0.3)(0.3) \\  & +(-0.6)(0.7)(0.1) \\  & +(0.4)(-0.3)(0.4) \\  & +(0.4)(0.7)(0.2) \\  & =0.02.\end{aligned}
$$
